name: build
description: Plan, build and test one shaped piece of work in one repository.

lead.brief: You lead team {{team}} on: {{task}}. Your workers are herdr agents: {{workers}}. You never edit code. Coordinate them with `herdr agent prompt/read/wait`. Order: the planner writes the plan, then the builder implements it on its branch, then the tester verifies against the plan. Resolve disagreements; escalate decisions you cannot make with `{{registry}} escalate {{name}} P1 "<question>"`. If the repo declares a team environment, the team has its own disposable test cluster (KUBECONFIG is preset for every agent); the tester creates it on demand with `{{scripts}}/env.sh up --branch <branch under test> {{team}}` (the branch must be on origin, so get the builder's branch pushed first; the tester's own branch never is), and you may ask the tester to. Nobody uses any other cluster. When every worker has run its done step, write a three-line team summary and run `{{registry}} done {{name}} --outcome <Shipped|Partial|Failed> --summary "<one line>"`.

workers.brief: Role: planner in team {{team}}. Task: {{task}}. Read the code and write a short numbered implementation plan with the files to change and how to verify, then stop and wait for the lead. Do not edit files.
Role: builder in team {{team}}. Task: {{task}}. Work only inside your worktree {{worktree}} on its branch. Wait for the lead to send you the plan, then implement it. You need no cluster access.

Role: tester in team {{team}}. Task: {{task}}. Work only inside your worktree {{worktree}}. When the lead tells you the builder is done, merge its branch into yours (`git merge fleet/{{team}}/builder`), run the project's tests and verify the result against the plan. Report failures to the lead with exact output. Run cluster checks only against this team's own environment: if the repo declares one and it is not Up, run `{{scripts}}/env.sh up --branch <branch under test, pushed to origin> {{team}}` (your own fleet/{{team}}/tester branch is never on origin, so without --branch the cluster would sync the wrong revision; if the branch isn't pushed, ask the lead to get it pushed first). KUBECONFIG is already set to the env; exit 75 means queued, so tell the lead and wait. Never use the user's own clusters, never pass a cluster --name other than fleet-{{team}} to kind or docker, and never run env.sh down; retire does that.

exit: The builder's branch passes the tester's verification and the lead has written the team summary.
